implementation_notes: The JMS 2.0 simplified API combines connection and session in JMSContext: the outbound adapter calls createProducer().send(queue, payload), the inbound one registers a MessageListener (or polls receive()) and maps the message onto the application interface. The application interface stays free of javax/jakarta.jms types; the provider owns connection pooling and reconnection, and acknowledgement mode is chosen on the context. Choose this variant when the deployment already has a JMS provider and no messaging framework.
pitfalls: A JMSContext is both connection and session and is not thread-safe: one context per thread (or container-managed injection) and application-managed contexts must be closed.
AUTO_ACKNOWLEDGE acknowledges when onMessage returns normally, so a caught-and-logged exception silently consumes the message.
onMessage runs on a provider thread: blocking calls or slow application work there starve message delivery for the whole session.

variants.name: Spring Integration channel adapters (declarative)
variants.implementation_notes: Spring Integration implements the EIP catalogue as framework components: an inbound channel adapter is a MessageProducerSupport that produces Messages from an external source, an outbound adapter is a MessageHandler that consumes from a channel, and protocol modules (JMS, AMQP, Kafka, file, mail) register ready-made adapter factories. The adapter code shrinks to the application-facing translation inside the flow (or to a custom MessageProducerSupport when no module exists). Choose it when a Spring context and an integration flow are already in place; the framework then owns pollers, error channels and transaction syncing.
pitfalls: Polling inbound adapters need a PollerMetadata/task scheduler; without tuning, a poller becomes the throughput limit and an unhandled error silently stops the source.
Application code that accepts framework Message<?> parameters re-couples the application to Spring Integration; translate to application types inside the flow.
